description: This bar chart, from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” illustrates the “effect” (y-axis, ranging from 0 to 20 with major ticks at intervals of 5) of different multilingual BERT models on four linguistic categories—“case,” “gender,” “number,” and “tense”—plotted along the x-axis under the label “tag.” Each category displays grouped bars representing six model variants: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red), as indicated in the legend. Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. For “case,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ show the highest effects (~12–11), followed by mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ (~5–6), while the R₂ variants are lower (~2–3). For “gender,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ again lead (~4), with mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ around ~1–2, and R₂ variants near ~1. In “number,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ are highest (~3), with others near ~1. For “tense,” all models show very low effects (~0–1), with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ slightly above zero. The chart suggests that B₂ variants generally outperform L₂ and R₂ across categories, especially for case and gender, while all models perform poorly on tense.
